question.text: A circle $C$ of radius 2 lies in the second quadrant and touches both the coordinate axes. Let $r$ be the radius of a circle that has centre at the point $(2,5)$ and intersects the circle $C$ at exactly two points. If the set of all possible values of r is the interval $(\alpha, \beta)$, then $3 \beta-2 \alpha$ is equal to :

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & C_1 C_2=\sqrt{(2+2)^2+(5-2)^2} \\ & =\sqrt{16+9} \\ & =5 \\ & r+2>5 \\ & r>3 \\ & r < 5+2 \\ & r < 7 \\ & \therefore \alpha=3, \beta=7 \\ & 3 \beta-2 \alpha=3(7)-2(3)=21-6=15\end{aligned}$
